test_name: learning_events Throughput (target: match/exceed previous best 605 ev/s, goal 5000 ev/s)

environment.learning_java: 1 replica, 200 Tomcat threads, 1 CPU core, Disruptor enabled
environment.disruptor_config: RingBuffer 65536, batch 200, flush 500ms, MULTI producer, BLOCKING wait
environment.tidb: TiDB primary (shared infra), learning_events table with AUTO_RANDOM PK

root_cause_analysis.primary_bottleneck: BFF Java + learning-java synchronous HTTP proxy chain (thread-per-request). Each service has 200 Tomcat threads limited to 1 CPU core on single-node VM.
root_cause_analysis.secondary_bottleneck: Disruptor consumer (DbLearningEventConsumer) uses synchronous batch DB write - drains ~300-500 ev/s, cannot keep up with higher ingress rates
root_cause_analysis.thread_pool_saturation: At 200+ users, BFF Tomcat thread pool (200 threads) saturates - requests queue, latency spikes, throughput drops
root_cause_analysis.scaling_failure: Scaling learning-java to 2 replicas caused WORSE performance due to single-node CPU contention (each pod gets ~0.5 core instead of 1)
root_cause_analysis.single_node_constraint: Cannot achieve 5000 ev/s on single node - requires horizontal scaling across multiple nodes

attempted_solutions: Direct learning-java test (bypassing BFF proxy) - still capped at ~370 ev/s by Disruptor consumer DB write speed
Patched learning-java HPA maxReplicas to 3 - scaling to 2 replicas caused CPU contention, reverted to 1
wait_time tuning (between 0.02-0.08s) for controlled event rate
recommendation: Multi-node cluster: scale BFF (3+ replicas) + learning-java (3+ replicas) across nodes. Consider async Disruptor consumer with separate DB writer thread pool. Pre-existing OutboxRelay SQL grammar bug should be fixed.
